source: segmentation (Blender simulation, background replaced by white)
time_convention: t = frame / 25; frame 0 at t = 0; frame i = round(t * 25)
pixel_convention: x right, y down, origin top-left, full-resolution pixels

camera.motion: static (rock mask centroid varies < 2 px, bbox edges <= 1 px over all 75 frames)
camera.view: high, steeply downward-looking oblique view: the person is seen from above (head/shoulders and white shirt visible, legs below); no horizon, ground plane or vanishing points visible because the background is removed
camera.perspective_cues: none usable besides the objects themselves; image-down = toward the camera along the ground (for a downward-tilted camera). Person's apparent size is nearly constant (body height ~40 px early, ~39 px late), i.e. depth change during the clip is small compared with the camera distance.
camera.focal_length: unknown; estimate from given depth_info + a known size

objects.name: human
objects.description: small single walking person, white shirt/top, grey-dark trousers, at lower-left of image (x ~483-500, y ~785-905); casts a long dark shadow (~92 px) toward the upper right that is attached at the feet
objects.occlusion: never occluded; shadow is attached to the feet and was excluded from the body box
objects.reference_point: pelvis estimate: x = mean x of body pixels, y = head top + 0.55 * median body height (39 px); see notes

motion_summary_px.direction: steadily down the image with a slight rightward drift (walking roughly toward the camera)
motion_summary_px.speed_pattern: uniform within noise (no start/stop, no acceleration visible)

body_height_head_top_to_lowest_foot.note: oscillates with the gait: max (~43-44) at full stride, min (~33-35) when legs pass; minima near frames 0, 18, 35, 53, 70

objects.name: rock
objects.description: very large textured rock occupying the top centre/right of the frame, beige/white lit left side, dark shadowed right side
objects.note: seen from above; vertical (height) extent cannot be separated from horizontal extent in this view. The rock's origin is assumed near its 3D centre; the mask centroid is its visible centre.

events.note: already walking at frame 0 and still walking at frame 74; no start/stop
approximate, from body-height minima; step period ~17.5 frames (0.7 s)

events.event: no contact between human and rock
events.note: human stays > 250 px from the rock outline; human moves away from the rock (down the image)

pairwise_image_distances_px.note: 2D image distances only; 3D distances need depth_info and a focal length
